 Game 5: IU basketball vs. Arkansas preview
 Alex Bozich 
 13 hours ago 
 0 
 Arkansas Athletics 
 The 2026-27 IU basketball season enters a pivotal week as the Hoosiers play two notable neutral-court contests. Up first: Arkansas at Madison Square Garden. 
 The Razorbacks are 3-1. Tipoff is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET on Peacock and NBC Sports Network. 
 Game information
 Who: Indiana (4-0) vs. Arkansas (3-1)
 Where: Madison Square Garden, New York, NY
 When: Tuesday, November 17, 2026, 7:30 p.m. EST
 TV: Peacock/NBCSN, Paul Burmeister (Play-by-Play), Robbie Hummel (Analyst), Carolina Pineda (Sideline)
 Radio: Don Fischer (Play-By-Play), Errek Suhr (Analyst)
 All-time series: Arkansas leads 3-2
 Last meeting: Arkansas 71, Indiana 64 on December 29, 2019, in Bloomington
 The line: Arkansas -2.5, O/U 154.5 (DraftKings)
 KenPom prediction: Arkansas 79, Indiana 77 (44 percent chance of an IU win)
 After four wins in the first two weeks of the 2026-27 season, the Hoosiers will try to build a non-conference resume this week with two neutral-court games. Indiana plays Arkansas tonight in New York City before taking on Kentucky on Friday night in Indianapolis.
 Tonight’s game is one of several for the Hoosiers this season on Peacock . If you are a YouTubeTV, Xfinity or FuboTV subscriber, Peacock games are typically available on NBC Sports Network.
 The Razorbacks are looking for their first resume win of the season under John Calipari, now in his third season in Fayetteville. Arkansas has wins against Arkansas Pine Bluff, Robert Morris and Central Arkansas and a neutral-court loss to Virginia.
 Meet the Razorbacks
 Arkansas began the season ranked No. 12 in the Associated Press top 25 poll but lost by 19 points to Virginia on November 8 at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C.
 There’s plenty to like about Arkansas’s long-term potential, thanks to a stellar freshman class that was among the nation’s best in the 2026 recruiting cycle. It may take a while for things to come together for the Razorbacks, but Tuesday offers a chance to show the progress made since the Virginia loss.
 Arkansas is a perimeter-led offense through four games, as all three of its double-figure scorers are guards or wings. The Razorbacks, however, are a low-3-point-volume group, attempting only 31.1 percent of their field goals from beyond the 3-point line. Indiana is attempting 43.6 percent of its field goals from 3 in four games.
 Junior Jeremiah Wilkinson, a native of Powder Springs, Georgia, began his career at Cal, played at Georgia last season and is now a Razorback. The 6-foot-1 guard made 60 3s as a freshman at Cal, 79 3s last season at Georgia and is 13-for-28 on 3s through four games. Wilkinson is the only Arkansas player who has made more than four 3-pointers this season. His 14.5 points per game lead the team, and 65 percent of his field-goal attempts this season have been 3s.
 Memphis native Billy Richmond III signed with Kentucky in the 2024 recruiting class but followed Calipari to Arkansas and is now in his third season with the Razorbacks. Richmond, a junior, is 6-foot-7 and puts a ton of pressure on the defense as a cutter and offensive rebounder. He’s shooting 74 percent at the rim and 65.6 percent from two-point range over four games. Richmond is second on the roster in scoring at 14 points per game.
 Jordan Smith Jr., one of the top players nationally in the 2026 class, is the third Arkansas player averaging in double figures. The 6-foot-2, left-handed freshman isn’t a shooter but is a tenacious defender (2.5 steals per game), can get to the bucket at will, and is an elite transition player. Smith is also shooting 74 percent at the rim but is making only 32 percent of his 2s outside of the cylinder. Given IU’s struggles to keep dribble penetration from reaching the paint, look for Smith to attack the rim relentlessly.
 Another freshman guard, 6-foot-2 Davion Thompson, comes off the bench and averages eight points and a team-high 5.5 assists. Thompson is coming off an eight-assist and one-turnover performance against Central Arkansas. He’s a solid midrange player and can make the 3-pointer, too.
 The Razorbacks start 7-foot freshman Miikka Muurinen and 6-foot-11 senior Cooper Bowser up front. Muurinen, a native of Finland, has been up and down through his first four games. He’s scored in double figures three times but is 2-for-11 on 3s and has eight turnovers. He’s taken 20 free throws in four games and is averaging 8.8 points and 3.5 rebounds in 19 minutes per game.
 Bowser played the last three seasons at Furman and is an efficient finisher who can rebound and block shots. Bowser is 14-for-18 on 2s (nine dunks), with 10 offensive rebounds and five blocks. He’ll give up size to Samet Yigitoglu, but he’s more agile and athletic.
 You can also expect to see freshman forward JJ Andrews, freshman guard Abdou Toure and freshman big man Maper Maker.
 The 6-foot-6 Andrews, who is from Little Rock, was the No. 17 player in the final 247Sports Composite rankings for 2026 and is a physical wing with an impressive wingspan who can score. He’s averaging 4.3 points in 17 minutes per game but should blossom as the season continues.
 Toure was the No. 14 player in the 2026 class and is averaging eight points on 57.1 percent shooting from the field in 14.3 minutes per game.
 Maker, an Australian native, is a developmental prospect but is getting minutes (14.3 per game) at the five as a backup. He’s pulling down 3.5 rebounds per game but has only attempted three shots.
 Keys to the game
 • Will Indiana’s defense be able to contain the perimeter talent of Arkansas?  The Arkansas roster is full of perimeter pieces who can get downhill and into the paint. The Hoosiers have been shaky defensively through four games, particularly in keeping dribble penetration out of the paint. The Razorbacks are quick, athletic and will attack the paint.
 • Indiana will need to make 3s : Arkansas is forcing turnovers (20 percent defensive turnover percentage), ranks in the top five nationally in block percentage (22.2) and does a good job limiting second-chance opportunities. The Hoosiers will take more 3s than Arkansas and need to create a scoring advantage from the perimeter.
 • The rebounding battle looms large : The rebounding battle will be fascinating to watch. Both teams have elite frontcourt size and go hard to the offensive glass. The team that creates more second-chance opportunities should feel good about its chances of leaving Madison Square Garden with a win.
 What it comes down to
 The KenPom projection is Arkansas by two, with a 44 percent chance of a Hoosier victory. Bart Torvik views it as a toss-up, favoring Arkansas by one with a 49 percent chance of an IU win.
 This will be IU’s stiffest test of the season so far, including the exhibition season. Arkansas is very much a work in progress and will be a completely different team in a few months. If the Razorbacks put it together for 40 minutes, they can play with anyone.
 Indiana’s guards have to play well and its rim protection must be much stronger than the first four games. This matchup will be a good litmus test for Darian DeVries to see where his team is just a few weeks into the season.
